claims.text: The hierarchical heterostructure contains multiscale grain-boundary networks.
The hierarchical heterostructure contains nanoscale phase inhomogeneities.
The multiscale grain boundaries and nanoscale phase inhomogeneities critically influence the alloy's mechanical behavior.
AE signatures and imaging descriptors can capture relevant phase distributions, grain boundaries, and crack-precursor features in HfNbTiVAl10.
These captured heterostructural features mediate correlations between microstructural events and macroscopic mechanical properties.
High-frequency acoustic emission data capture rapid microstructural damage events such as localized yielding.
High-frequency acoustic emission data capture early crack formation.
High-resolution microstructural imaging provides descriptors of static structural features relevant to mechanical response.
Fusing AE features and imaging descriptors in a machine-learning surrogate enables rapid prediction of Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture-initiation thresholds.
The hybrid model can make these predictions without running computationally intensive full-field simulations for each estimate.
The hybrid approach will reduce prediction errors for Young's modulus by approximately 15–20% relative to established simulations.
The hybrid approach will reduce prediction errors for yield strength by approximately 15–20% relative to established simulations.
The hybrid approach will reduce prediction errors for fracture-initiation thresholds by approximately 15–20% relative to established simulations.
The hybrid approach will produce estimates on the order of minutes.
Conventional full-scale finite-element and phase-field simulations require extensive computational resources and longer processing times for this hierarchical alloy.
Excessive AE noise or overlapping AE events may prevent association of signals with specific microstructural triggers.
Insufficient imaging frequency or resolution may fail to capture transient damage evolution, especially at high strain rates.
Noise filtering and synchronization variability can affect the model's predictive performance.
